items.titleZh: Does Google even want to win at AI?
items.descriptionZh:
谷歌正在经历一场重大的人工智能部门重组，这一消息在科技行业引发了关于“谷歌是否正在输掉AI竞赛”的激烈讨论。上周，谷歌宣布将其AI部门Google DeepMind进行结构性调整：公司首席科学家杰夫·迪恩（Jeff Dean）离开谷歌，自己创业成立一家新实验室；DeepMind联合创始人兼CEO德米斯·哈萨比斯（Demis Hassabis）则卸任CEO，转任DeepMind董事长，专注于更长远的科学研究。这次高管变动被外界解读为谷歌在AI前沿竞争中处于被动局面后的应对措施。

从背景来看，谷歌本来拥有赢得AI竞赛的最佳条件：庞大的用户基础、强大的搜索分发能力、海量数据、顶级研究人才和雄厚的资本。在OpenAI与马斯克的诉讼材料中甚至显示，业界一直对哈萨比斯心怀敬畏。然而现实是，谷歌在生成式AI浪潮中反应迟缓，被OpenAI和Anthropic等后来者反超。在这次访谈中，《The Verge》资深AI记者海登·菲尔德（Hayden Field）与分析家们一致认为，谷歌目前确实落后了，但绝不能忽视其巨大的“安全垫”——比如Search、云服务、TPU等基础设施，以及数亿用户的日常使用场景。菲尔德比喻道，谷歌像一个“信托基金宝宝”，即使犯了巨大错误，凭借其资源和积累，也很难被彻底淘汰。

关于这次重组的深层原因，菲尔德指出，哈萨比斯一直对产品化不感兴趣，他更关注世界模型、蛋白质折叠、药物发现等长期研究；杰夫·迪恩也类似，他曾在离职前公开反对大规模监控、支持AI伦理红线，甚至签署支持Anthropic的法庭之友简报。当这些“道德领袖”离开后，谷歌内部的价值观体系可能出现真空。接替哈萨比斯的是科拉伊·卡瓦库科格鲁（Koray Kavukcuoglu），但他被认为是一个“产品型”领导者，更擅长加速产品迭代，而不是在道德问题上发声。多位谷歌员工向菲尔德透露，迪恩的离开让许多人感到士气低落，也加剧了此前的“人才外流”，未来几个月可能还有更多人出走。

这次变动还引发了关于“前沿研究”与“产品化”之间的长期矛盾。SemiAnalysis在分析报告中直言：“我们认为DeepMind已不再是前沿实验室，谷歌达到最先进水平的概率已降为零。”尽管该机构承认谷歌不太可能永远无法回到SOTA，但他们认为谷歌的正统文化——极度官僚、缓慢、战略上畏首畏尾——才是根本问题。菲尔德对此持保留态度，她认为“降为零”有点夸张，但谷歌确实可能会陷入“永远在追赶”的循环：当其他实验室投入长期研究、探索新方向时，谷歌只能不断复制对手的成果，而无法再次引领。

访谈中还提到了谷歌CEO桑达尔·皮查伊（Sundar Pichai）的回应。在Google I/O上，皮查伊曾表示，将Brain和DeepMind合并为Google DeepMind并非易事，就像“把斯坦福和MIT合并成一个系”。他承认谷歌最初没有为AI时刻做好准备，但现在决心重新组织，建立核心模型和基础设施团队。当被问及“站在奇点山脚”这个说法时，皮查伊透露他和哈萨比斯对AGI的讨论很多，谷歌实际上正在制定对奇点/AGI的官方定义，其概念与OpenAI和微软合同中的定义相似：“一个在大多数经济价值工作上超越人类的高度自主系统”。这一定义在业界已流传多年，而哈萨比斯之所以聚焦于健康、生物和世界模型，正是他个人对AGI的理解——希望解决科学和医学问题，而不仅仅是让AI写代码或优化商业流程。

这实际上揭示了谷歌内部的一个关键结构性矛盾：要让AI产生当下经济价值，最直接的是用于写软件、自动化企业流程、代理购物等“无聊”功能；而哈萨比斯所追求的是更宏大、更长期的“奇点”愿景。这种产品与研究的张力在OpenAI和Anthropic身上同样存在，但谷歌作为一家上市公司，还承担着股东对短期回报的压力。皮查伊在声明中称谷歌“承诺处于前沿”，但哈萨比斯的表述“我们拥有从此刻开始领先的要素”被解读为“我们尚未领先，但未来或可做到”——两人都间接承认当前谷歌不在第一梯队。

对于谷歌战略的另一种解读是，它可能不再执着于必须亲自站在最前沿。谷歌云业务正在爆炸式增长，它甚至愿意把自家TPU和算力卖给Anthropic、OpenAI等直接竞争对手，扮演“卖水人”的角色。如果Gemini模型只能做到“足够好”，足以支持搜索、Gmail、AI概览和免费让用户“用AI vibe coding建网站”，而真正的颠覆性AGI由其他实验室推动，谷歌作为基础设施供应商同样能赚取巨额利润。菲尔德认为，目前谷歌仍会继续追求前沿，因为投资者需要这样的叙事来推高股价，但如果人才流失持续、追赶乏力，未来一两年内转向“稳坐第二梯队、专注卖算力”的模式绝非不可能。

关于具体模型性能，访谈提到Gemini 3在发布后曾短暂登顶模型排行榜，但很快被更先进的模型超越。即将推出的Gemini 4被寄予厚望，但SemiAnalysis的评论“这些行动不是对Gemini 4 Pro感到兴奋的人会做的”表明，连内部高管都对它缺乏信心。谷歌在Google I/O上重推3.5系列模型，但该系列并未处于领先位置，落后幅度不小。菲尔德认为，评判谷歌是否成功，可以看每次发布的新模型究竟有多少真正的创新，还是只是几个月前对手已经做过的事；此外也要观察DeepMind工程师的离职潮，以及哈萨比斯最终是否彻底离开（现在是过渡期）。如果Gemini 4发布后连一两周的“领先期”都没有，甚至在基准测试中表现平平，那么谷歌可能真的陷入了“永远追赶”的困境。

最后，访谈还触及了地缘政治和商业伦理问题。谷歌与特朗普政府的关系、允许国防部使用AI、放弃此前“不将AI用于军事”的承诺，这些举动让许多重视价值观的技术人才感到失望。OpenAI和Anthropic也面临类似的道德困境，但不少谷歌和OpenAI的员工流向Anthropic，因为那里至少在表面上更注重AI安全与社会责任。菲尔德总结道，谷歌输掉“AI竞赛”的可能性不大，但它可能改变获胜的定义——不再追求成为AGI的缔造者，而是成为AGI时代最重要的算力和云服务供应商。无论哪种结局，这场组织变革都将深刻影响全球AI研究的格局。

items.title: Geekom IT13 Max 2026 review: Meteor Lake rides again in a $799 mini PC
items.description: Geekom mates an Intel Meteor Lake Core Ultra 9 processor with soldered 24GB DDR5 dual-channel RAM to conjure up an attractively specified and priced mini PC for the RAMpocalypse era.
items.content: The strategy of using last-gen laptop parts in mini PCs used to mean excellent performance at competitive prices. At least, it did until the RAMpocalypse swept across tech. Nevertheless, Geekom is pushing the idea that its IT13 Max, using a Core Ultra 9 185H at $799, offers a value option in mid-2026. Looking at some of the other prices for mini PCs we’ve seen recently, it might be right.Other than the reasonable Ultra 9 tier price for the performance, RAM and storage in the current market, Geekom delivers a very competent mini PC here. It looks like an unassuming, business-like machine from the outside, but has plenty of ports, easy internal access, and is very sturdy.Design of the Geekom IT13 Max 2026 Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Geekom’s new IT13 Max 2026 follows a very traditional NUC design. With its just-under-a-liter volume, this black device is just slightly bigger in every dimension than the MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG (0.8 L), and shares a lot of the matte dark understated design and subtle branding of that unit. Later on, you’ll notice this pair has a lot in common when it comes to performance, too, despite being two Intel generations apart and featuring a huge price gap.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Geekom uses a matte plastic outer shell here, but the perforated venting areas to the sides and removable bottom plate are metal, as is an inner chassis. It is pretty easy to get into the IT13 Max, as there are just four screws positioned in the center of the rubber feet.Users have access to power and headphones on the front panel, and a wide range of fast USB, networking, and monitor connection options. Geekom hasn’t implemented any biometrics in the power button, for example, and also eschews the addition of a Copilot button.Geekom IT13 Max 2026 Specifications Swipe to scroll horizontally Processor Intel Core Ultra 9 185H (16C/22T), up to 5.1 GHz, 45W Graphics Intel Arc integrated graphics using eight Xe cores RAM 24GB LPDDR5 (8x 3GB ICs, soldered, dual‑channel) Storage 500GB Kingston NV3 PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD and spare M.2 2242 slot Physical Ports Front: 4 × USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type‑A (front, one S5 Always On), 3.5 mm audio jack. Sides: SD Card 4.0, Kensington Lock, Rear: 1x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type‑A, 1x USB 2.0 Type‑A, 2x USB4 (both with DP-Alt, one with Power in), 2x RJ‑45 2.5 Gbps, 2x HDMI 2.0, DC‑in barrel jack Wireless Intel Wi-Fi 7 + Bluetooth 5.4 Dimensions 5.35 x 5.20 x 2.13 inches (≈ 0.97 L chassis) Operating System Windows 11 Pro 25H2 Price (as configured) $799 Today's best Geekom IT13 Max 2026 deals No price informationCheck Amazon No price informationCheck Best BuyWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricesPorts and Upgradeability on the Geekom IT13 Max 2026 Image 1 of 8 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 8 View Original Image 2 of 8 View Original Image 3 of 8 View Original Image 4 of 8 View Original Image 5 of 8 View Original Image 6 of 8 View Original Image 7 of 8 View Original Image 8 of 8 View Original When I decided to look inside, two of the four rubber feet could be unscrewed by hand, but another pair were just a little too tight, so I had to reach for my Phillips-head screwdriver. Once you get into this Geekom mini PC, there’s not much you can do, as the RAM is soldered.The only upgrades users have access to are swapping the installed M.2 devices. There’s an M.2 2280 SSD slot with the NVMe PCIe4 500GB Kingston drive and thermal pad in place. Under that is the system’s M.2 2230 wireless connectivity card. To the side of these, I saw a vacant M.2 2242 slot. Oddly, the spec sheet I got from Geekom mentioned 2.5-inch SATA SSD/HDD expansion options, and not M.2 2242. There seemed to be an unused SATA header area on the motherboard, so perhaps specs were changed at a late stage of development.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe system offers a good array of ports built-in, and I didn’t want or need to reach for a docking solution during testing.On the front of this mini PC, there is a generous row of four USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A ports. One of these supports always-on smart device charging. Next to these ports is a 3.5 mm audio jack and an inset power button with a white LED to indicate it is powered up.On the left side, there is a full-size SD card reader, and on the right, you will find a Kensington lock slot.At the rear of the IT13 Max 2026, there’s a series of vents, and below them, most of the I/O. This includes a USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A port, a USB 2.0 Type-A, two USB4 Type-C (both with DP-Alt, one offers Power in), two RJ-45 2.5 Gbps Ethernet ports, a pair of HDMI 2.0 ports, and a DC‑in barrel jack for the supplied power brick.Test System Setup Swipe to scroll horizontally System CPU (i)GPU Memory Chassis GMKtec EVO-T2 Intel Core Ultra X7 358H (16C/16T: 4P + 8E + 4 LPE), up to 4.8 GHz Intel Arc B390 (Xe3, 12 cores, up to 2.5 GHz) 2x 32GB LPDDR5X-8533 soldered Dual-fan,1.72 liters MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG Intel Core Ultra 9 386H (16C/16T: 6P + 8E + 2LPE), up to 4.9 GHz Intel Graphics (Xe3, 4 Cores, up to 2.5 GHz) 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 Sodimm Single fan, 0.52 liters Geekom A9 Max 2026 AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 (12C / 24T: 4x Zen 5 , 8x Zen 5c), up to 5.2 GHz Radeon 890M (RDNA 3.5, 16 CUs, up to 3.1 GHz) 1x 32GB DDR5-5600 Sodimm Single fan, 0.82 liters Arctic Senza AI 370 AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (12C / 24T: 4x Zen 5 , 8x Zen 5c), up to 5.1 GHz Radeon 890M (RDNA 3.5, 16 CUs, up to 2.9 GHz) 2x 16GB LPDDR5X‑8000 soldered Passive, 4.82 liters Beelink SER10 MAX AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 (12C / 24T: 4x Zen 5 , 8x Zen 5c), up to 5.2 GHz Radeon 890M (RDNA 3.5, 16 CUs, up to 3.1 GHz) 2x 32GB DDR5-5600 Sodimm Single fan, 0.81 liters Geekom IT13 Max 2026 Intel Core Ultra 9 185H (16C/22T: 6P + 8E + 2 LPE), up to 5.1 GHz Intel Arc graphics (Xe-LPG, 8 cores, up to 2.35 GHz) 2x 16GB DDR5-5600 Soldered Single fan, 0.97 liters GMKtec Evo-X3 AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (16C/32T: 16x Zen 5), up to 5.1 GHz Radeon 8060S (RDNA 3.5, 40 CUs, up to 2.9 GHz) 2x 64GB LPDDR5X-8000 Soldered Triple-fan, 2.69 liters Productivity Performance on the Geekom IT13 Max 2026Geekom boasts of all-round flagship performance from this new mini PC and thankfully skips any outlandish AI-related claims. Now we are getting down to testing, we shall see if there are any glaring weaknesses that come from choosing Intel’s previous-previous-gen silicon.Geekom has opted for older silicon in the IT13 Max 2026, utilizing Intel’s Core Ultra 9 185H (16C/22T), which boosts up to 5.1 GHz, and shares die space with an Arc iGPU featuring eight Xe cores. This is quite a lot of compute and GPU resources in a little SoC, and that’s why the Ultra 9 185H was one of the top mobile processors a couple of years ago. There’s an NPU on board, too, but it can only muster 11 TOPS according to Intel’s data sheets. The question is if that chip, alongside 24GB of RAM and a 500GB, still stands up. Image 1 of 8 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 8 View Original Image 2 of 8 View Original Image 3 of 8 View Original Image 4 of 8 View Original Image 5 of 8 View Original Image 6 of 8 View Original Image 7 of 8 View Original Image 8 of 8 View Original Image 1 of 11 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 11 View Original Image 2 of 11 View Original Image 3 of 11 View Original Image 4 of 11 View Original Image 5 of 11 View Original Image 6 of 11 View Original Image 7 of 11 View Original Image 8 of 11 View Original Image 9 of 11 View Original Image 10 of 11 View Original Image 11 of 11 View Original In the comparison charts above, you can see how the IT13 Max squared up to more modern rivals. In Cinebench 2026, Maxon’s current-gen CPU rendering benchmark, the single-thread result of ~450 points does mean that the Meteor Lake machine does trail the pack, but it isn’t a disaster. Turning to the multicore result in the same test, the latest Geekom mini PC with its older “Meteor Lake” chip basically matches the MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG based on Intel “Panther Lake” silicon. Admittedly, the former’s 16C/22T core/thread count and higher power limits lift it against the Intel Core Ultra 9 386H with 16C/16T in the MSI.In HandBrake, the Geekom managed 13 frames per second on our standard video transcoding test. That’s neck and neck with the MSI, again, but only with very long videos would you likely notice how it lags behind.Gaming and Graphics on the Geekom IT13 Max 2026The Geekom IT13 Max isn't hopeless in gaming, but it sits in the lower portion of our mini PC game benchmark comparison tables. It mostly performs better than the MSI Panther Lake mini PC, again. Not bad for something from two generations prior.For my traditional spell of gaming fun before serious benchmarking, I decided to go on a quick adventure in Borderlands GOTY Enhanced (2019). The game ran at an average of about 80 frames per second when using the High preset at 1080p. I didn’t have any problem with frame rates mostly in the 80s, periodic dips in the frame chart looked worse than they actually felt during the game. It is definitely an older game now, and while the iGPU ran at close to its max utilization on my uncapped frame rate run, the CPU was barely burdened. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original I also ran a few synthetic gaming benchmarks, a trio of 3DMark tests. One of those was the cross-platform 3DMark Solar Bay, which is well-weighted for iGPU performance comparisons, delivering playable frame rates on this type of graphics hardware.The Geekom IT13 Max 2026 earned a score of 13,430 in this test. The Meteor Lake mini PC’s score (with eight Xe-LPG) cores is about 18% faster than the newer Panther Lake rival (with four Xe3-LPG cores). Both of them, and the AMD Ryzen AI mini PCs we have tested crumble in comparison with the GMKtec Evo-T2 with the best Panther Lake iGPU, the 12 Xe3-LPG core B390.Moving onto some popular AAA gaming titles, I next checked how Shadow of the Tomb Raider performed on the Geekom. Its average of 37 and minimum of 29 frames per second put it once more very squarely in the same territory as the MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG mini PC.Cyberpunk 2077 was technically playable using the Steam Deck 1080p preset that we have been using for mini PC comparisons. Its average and 1% low results were 36 and 30 frames per second, respectively. Very slightly behind the Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG this time by both those metrics. Running Cyberpunk 2077 at 1080p using the high preset (no upscaling tech) is not recommended, as the IT13 Max achieved an average of 21 frames per second.The overall picture that emerged was that the Geekom IT13 Max 2026 isn’t bad at modern gaming with low-ish settings, with upscaling if available, but is more suited to lighter and older titles.Power, Heat, and Noise when using the Geekom IT13 Max 2026I tested the IT13 Max 2026 with the default power profile Geekom shipped it with, which is a Processor Base Power (PBP, PL1) of 45W, a Maximum Turbo Power (MTP, PL2) of 70W, and a PL4 of 120W, according to system information tools. During testing, I measured total system power consumption with a plug-in power meter, as well as reading the CPU temperatures using a Windows utility. Image 1 of 2 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 2 View Original Image 2 of 2 View Original At low load, with Google Docs open for typing among a few other browser tabs, the system consistently pulled around 14W. At the same time, the CPU temperature would stick around 43 degrees Celsius.During prolonged stress testing of the IT13 Max 2026, the highest wattage consumed by the whole system momentarily spiked to around 85W, but a stable sustained level of ~70W was generally observed. It also seemed to stabilize at approximately the 70 degrees Celsius level after initially climbing higher. Thermal pic taken under load with system tools reporting a CPU temperature of ~70 degrees Celsius. (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)The Geekom is a quiet mini PC, but you can hear the small cooling fan blowing clearly if it is put through any demanding CPU or GPU task. My meter showed 29.8 dB when idling, which is good, but the noise level ramped to a more than noticeable 52.3 dB when the system was under a sustained load.Software and Warranty on the Geekom IT13 Max 2026This mini PC came with Windows 11 Pro preinstalled and activated. As usual, before testing, we ensured Windows and drivers were fully up to date.There were no utilities added by Geekom. Checking the Installed Apps list on Windows revealed both Realtek Audio Console and Realtek Card Reader as the only non-standard components in a typical Windows install.Linux is also fully supported, according to the official spec sheets.Geekom sells the IT13 Max 2026 with a three-year warranty, though the company does require you to pay a return shipping fee.Geekom IT13 Max 2026 configurationsGeekom sells just one configuration of the IT13 Max 2026 — the one we have tested with 24GB of soldered LPDDR5 RAM and a 500GB SSD preinstalled.Those browsing and interested in this particular configuration should be careful, though. Geekom is still selling an older variant of the IT13 Max with very similar specs but with two SODIMM slots, making it expandable to 96GB of DDR5-5600 memory. This other Core Ultra 9 185H device comes with a single 16GB SODIMM and a 1TB SSD preinstalled. It is usually $899, but Geekom is currently selling this version for the same $799 if you prefer its RAM/SSD configuration.Bottom LineDuring my testing of the Geekom IT13 Max 2026, I found it to be a dependable device. In the current climate, the soldered dual-channel 24GB of RAM might be a sweet spot if you want your integrated GPU to access a decent chunk of the memory pool. It is interesting to see the prior IT Max model now moved down to the same $799 price if you don’t want to accept soldered RAM, would like more preinstalled storage, and are otherwise attracted to owning a tiny PC powered by Intel’s Core Ultra 9 185H with its 16C/22T and reasonable Arc iGPU.It is very interesting to see this mini PC match the far more modern MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG we tested recently (which costs far more, as is often the case for enterprise pricing) in many of the benchmark applications and games. The MSI uses a Core Ultra 9 386H, so this is a reasonably fair U9 vs U9 comparison. In practice, the Geekom even seemed to idle at a slightly lower wattage than the MSI, but admittedly, it would pull around 70W under load, which is 15W more than the MSI Panther Lake was observed consuming. This points to one of the biggest attractions of most mainstream Panther Lake CPUs being their efficiency, which is far more important in a laptop than a mini PC like this.To conclude, this does indeed seem like a capable, moderately quiet under light day-to-day loads, and power-efficient offering for the ticket price in mid-2026. At $799 the prior model might offer some of the best competition if removable RAM, albeit just 16GB, and a 1TB preinstalled SSD can sway you.Geekom IT13 Max 2026: Price Comparison No price informationCheck Amazon No price informationCheck Best BuyWe check over 250 million products every day for the best pricespowered by

items.titleZh: Geekom IT13 Max 2026 review: Meteor Lake rides again in a $799 mini PC
items.descriptionZh:
在内存价格持续走高、硬件成本普遍攀升的背景下，Geekom逆势推出了基于英特尔上一代移动处理器的迷你主机IT13 Max 2026，试图在2026年中期以799美元的价位提供一款兼顾性能与性价比的产品。这款设备搭载的是Core Ultra 9 185H，这是英特尔“Meteor Lake”代的旗舰级移动芯片，拥有16核22线程，最高加速频率5.1GHz，默认基础功耗45W，集成了8个Xe核心的Arc核显，并附带算力仅11 TOPS的NPU。虽然芯片并非最新，但在当前内存价格高企的市场中，799美元能买到这样的CPU、24GB内存和500GB SSD配置，确实具备一定吸引力。

从外观设计来看，IT13 Max 2026采用了非常传统的NUC风格，机身容积不到一升，约为0.97升，比MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG略大一圈。外壳为磨砂黑色塑料材质，但侧面通风区域和可拆卸底板是金属，内部还有金属框架来提升结构强度。拆解很方便，只需拧下橡胶脚垫中央的四颗螺丝。前面板提供了电源键、耳机孔和四个USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A接口，其中一个支持智能设备常充（S5 Always On）；左侧有SD卡读卡器，右侧有Kensington锁孔；背部则配置了一个USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A、一个USB 2.0 Type-A、两个USB4 Type-C接口（均支持DP-Alt，其中一个支持电源输入）、两个2.5G RJ45网口、两个HDMI 2.0接口以及DC电源输入。无线方面支持Wi-Fi 7和蓝牙5.4。整体接口丰富，完全不需要扩展坞。

在内部扩展性上，这款迷你主机的内存是焊接在主板上的24GB LPDDR5（双通道），用户无法升级。唯一可更换的是存储设备：预装一块500GB Kingston NV3 PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD，占据一个M.2 2280插槽，旁边还有一个M.2 2230插槽用于无线网卡，还有一个空余的M.2 2242插槽。值得注意的是，官方规格表里提到支持2.5英寸SATA扩展，但主板上似乎只有一个闲置的SATA接口区域，实际并未提供安装位，推测是开发后期改动所致。

性能测试方面，Geekom IT13 Max 2026作为一台采用两代前处理器的迷你主机，表现并不差。在Cinebench 2026单线程测试中，约450分的成绩确实落后于现代的Rival，但多线程成绩基本上与采用英特尔最新“Panther Lake”架构的MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG持平——这得益于185H拥有更多的16核22线程和更高的功耗限制。在HandBrake视频转码测试中，该机取得了13帧每秒的成绩，与MSI几乎持平，只有在处理超长视频时才会感受到差距。游戏性能上，这款迷你主机处于我们游戏基准测试表的较低区间，但大多数时候还是优于MSI那款Panther Lake主机。实际体验《无主之地：年度加强版》在1080p高画质下平均约80帧，运行流畅。3DMark Solar Bay测试得分13,430分，比配备4个Xe3-LPG核心的MSI快了约18%。在《古墓丽影：暗影》中平均37帧、最低29帧，与MSI极为接近；《赛博朋克2077》在Steam Deck 1080p预设下平均36帧、最低1%为30帧，勉强可玩，但高画质下只有21帧。总体而言，这款产品适合以较低画质运行现代游戏，或者流畅运行较老、较轻量的游戏。

功耗和散热方面，Geekom默认设定PL1为45W、PL2为70W、PL4为120W。低负载（如打开谷歌文档和几个浏览器标签）时整机功耗约14W，CPU温度约43摄氏度；持续压力测试下整机功耗峰值瞬间冲到约85W，稳定在70W左右，温度最终稳定在约70摄氏度。噪音方面，待机时非常安静，实测29.8分贝，但持续负载下风扇声音明显明显攀升至52.3分贝，属于中规中矩的表现。

软件和保修方面，该机预装Windows 11 Pro并已激活，系统干净，没有额外预装工具，仅有两个Realtek驱动组件。官方宣称支持Linux。Geekom为IT13 Max 2026提供三年保修，但需要用户承担退货运费。目前官方只有一个配置版本，即用户测试的24GB焊接内存加500GB SSD，售价799美元。不过要注意，Geekom仍在销售旧版IT13 Max，外观和CPU几乎相同，但采用双SODIMM插槽，可扩展至96GB DDR5-5600，且预装1TB SSD和单条16GB内存。旧版通常售价899美元，但当前促销价也是799美元，如果用户更看重可升级内存和更大预装存储，旧版同样值得考虑。

综上所述，Geekom IT13 Max 2026是一台可靠的迷你主机。在当前内存价格高企的环境中，24GB焊接双通道内存能让集成显卡获得充足的显存带宽，是一个不错的配置平衡点。最令人印象深刻的是，它在许多基准测试和实际游戏中都能与配置Core Ultra 9 386H、价格昂贵得多的MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG一较高下。虽然满载功耗比MSI高出约15W，但这对于迷你主机来说并非大问题。对于2026年年中，799美元的价格带来了令人满意的性能、适中的噪音和不错的功耗表现。当然，如果你更在意内存可升级性，那么同价位的旧版IT13 Max也是一个强有力的竞争者。

自2025年末以来，内存、存储和显卡价格持续飙升，原本亲民的硬件逐渐变得高不可攀，消费者不得不依靠捆绑套餐来获取合理价格。在此背景下，Newegg近期推出了一组极具性价比的三件套组合：以658.99美元的价格，即可获得AMD旗舰级处理器Ryzen 9 9900X、华硕TUF Gaming X870E-Plus Wi-Fi 7主板以及16GB TeamGroup T-Force Vulkan DDR5-5200内存，并附赠一款Cooler Master 240mm一体式水冷散热器。该套餐原价932.98美元，折扣幅度达273.99美元（约29%），相当于白拿内存，这在当前高价环境下实属罕见。

核心组件方面，Ryzen 9 9900X采用台积电4nm FinFET工艺制造（I/O die为6nm），拥有12核心24线程，基础频率4.4GHz，最高加速频率5.6GHz，TDP仅120W，热管理相对轻松，并且由于处理器完全解锁超频，用户还可以在降压情况下继续挖掘额外频率余量。该芯片原生支持AVX-512指令集，与AM5平台向后兼容，强大的多线程与单线程性能使其非常适合那些既玩游戏又需要处理生产力任务的用户，能充分利用额外核心与线程。虽然AMD的非X3D系列处理器（如更大规模的Ryzen 9 9950X）此前已获得市场好评，9900X同样继承了这一优秀基因。

内存部分，这对DDR5-5200频率略低于AMD所推荐的甜点速度，但实际体验中若非紧盯帧率计数器，很难察觉性能差异。黑色无RGB设计也与主板风格相得益彰。若用户觉得16GB不足，还可再次购买同规格套件组成32GB，总成本也仅为240美元，依然比单独购买划算得多。

主板方面，华硕TUF Gaming X870E-Plus Wi-Fi 7是一款均衡的AM5平台产品：供电电路足以支撑旗舰级处理器，即使搭配组合中的9900X并超频也游刃有余；存储扩展配备4个M.2插槽（其中1个为PCIe 5.0）和2个SATA接口；网络方面集成Wi-Fi 7与2.5GbE有线网口；后置I/O提供了多达13个USB端口，包括两个USB4 40Gbps Type-C接口；音频方案采用上代Realtek旗舰解码ALC1220P，品质扎实。此外，华硕的AI优化套件（AI缓存加速、AI超频、AI散热II、AI网络II）以及DIY友好的设计，让装机与系统调校都更加便捷。

总体而言，这套以658.99美元（节省274美元）出售的AM5组合，是目前Newegg上颇具吸引力的优惠之一，尤其适合非X3D芯片用户。将内存价格折算为“免费”的促销方式并不常见，而且即使升级到32GB，总成本依然远低于单独购买，是一款适合游戏与多任务生产力的高性价比选择。

items.title: PBS broadcaster loses access to 50TB of data comprising 70 years of TV history after contracted cloud storage vendor goes defunct — public TV channel sues Iron Mountain data center, which hosts archival materials, to ensure preservation
items.description: Public broadcaster Nine PBS is in trouble after its cloud storage provider went out of business and it now can't access more than 50TB of archival data. The data center hosting the files can't simply turn over the files, as it's legally owned by another entity, even if the channel is the ultimate owner of the stored data.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 23 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nine PBS is afraid that it will lose over 70 years of archival materials and programming after its contracted cloud storage vendor has apparently gone out of business. According to Current, the channel used Open Source Storage, or OSS, for storing over 50TB of data — but it suddenly lost access to its data earlier this year. Nine PBS has been working with OSS and its predecessor since 2019 and intended to renew its contract on March 6 of this year. The company never responded and abruptly cut off the station’s data access even though it still had 30 days to retrieve its data after the contract ended.The station dug a little bit deeper when it discovered that the OSS website no longer existed and was listed as delinquent under the Colorado Secretary of State. It also discovered that OSS utilized Iron Mountain’s services, so it sent a demand letter to the latter to preserve its data and to "pay any reasonable costs associated with its demand." At the time, Iron Mountain did not confirm or deny that it possessed Nine PBS’ data.Go deeper with TH Premium: Memory (Image credit: SK Hynix)AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supplyThe future of DRAM: From DDR5 to future ICsHigh-bandwidth memory roadmapHere's why HBM is coming for your PC's RAMAt the same time, the channel also sued OSS and its leadership, which it paused after someone who claimed to be a "managing partner of the group that officially acquired" the company reached out. The person, named James Tramel, initially communicated with Nine PBS for about a month. However, this also ended abruptly, with the channel eventually receiving an automated reply from Tramel stating he is no longer connected with OSS. The channel was able to get in touch with him, and he said that he had "been defrauded" into acquiring the cloud storage company and that ownership and operations have now reverted to the previous owners.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: This left the channel at a loss, so it continued its case against OSS, and the court ruled that Nine PBS had all the rights to access its data stored with OSS and that the latter should "facilitate its transfer to a new vendor." The channel’s attorney also reached out to Iron Mountain to inform the company of the pending case in Colorado; Iron Mountain finally admitted to holding the data. Iron Mountain initially agreed to turn over Nine PBS’ data, but it eventually backtracked and claimed that OSS owned the data it stored. Because of this, Nine PBS now has no choice but to sue Iron Mountain, too, to ensure the data is not deleted.The entire thing is a nightmare scenario for Nine PBS, especially as it’s still unclear what will happen to its data. The channel can only assume that its former cloud storage provider is no longer paying data center bills, so it’s rightfully concerned that its data might end up lost forever. And even if Iron Mountain is willing to give Nine PBS its data, it risks getting sued by OSS — it is simply protecting itself by refusing to turn over the said stored data. You may like Farmer donates land for a park, city sells it for data center development Blackstone-owned QTS abandons planned world’s largest data center campus after years of lawsuits Gamers compress 80TB map of Minecraft's oldest anarchy server down to a 15TB download It seems that the safest legal way to resolve this issue is for Nine PBS to get a court order requiring Iron Mountain to turn over its data. But the channel must act quickly to ensure that its data, which Nine PBS VP and CCO Leah Freeman said to Current represented "70 years of our organization’s history," stays safe.It's not clear if the channel has backups of its data, but based on its determination, we suspect not. This is strange, though, especially for a major organization, as one can easily purchase a six-bay NAS on Amazon and populate it with the best HDDs. This also goes against the 3-2-1 backup rule, which says you should keep three copies of your files stored in two different mediums, with one of them running offsite. Hopefully Nine PBS will implement a better backup system once it regains access to its data. And at least there's still a chance — it's not like the fire that the South Korean government experienced last year, which saw 858TB of data go up in smoke.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsors Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.

items.titleZh: PBS broadcaster loses access to 50TB of data comprising 70 years of TV history after contracted cloud storage vendor goes defunct — public TV channel sues Iron Mountain data center, which hosts archival materials, to ensure preservation
items.descriptionZh:
位于美国密苏里州的公共电视台Nine PBS正面临一场数据灾难：其合作多年的云存储供应商Open Source Storage（OSS）疑似已经倒闭，导致电视台超过70年的历史档案可能永久丢失。这起事件不仅暴露了公共媒体在数据托管上的脆弱性，也引发了关于云存储外包、数据所有权以及备份策略的广泛讨论。

**事件背景与经过**  
Nine PBS自2019年起使用OSS及其前身服务来存储约50TB的节目资料和档案，双方合作一直延续至今年。按照计划，电视台应于2023年3月6日续签合同，但OSS方面始终未作回应，并且合同到期后仅过了30天数据取回期，电视台便突然失去了对数据的访问权限。更令人不安的是，Nine PBS随后发现OSS的官方网站已经无法访问，且该公司在科罗拉多州州务卿网站上被标记为“欠税违规”状态。进一步调查显示，OSS实际使用了Iron Mountain（铁山公司）的数据中心服务，于是Nine PBS向Iron Mountain发出正式函件，要求其保留数据并支付相关合理费用。Iron Mountain起初既未确认也未否认持有数据，但在后续沟通中逐步承认了数据确实存在，却又以“OSS拥有该数据”为由拒绝移交。这一反复无常的态度迫使Nine PBS在起诉OSS之后，又不得不将Iron Mountain一并告上法庭。

**法律与技术博弈**  
案件审理过程中，法庭已明确裁定Nine PBS对其存储在OSS的数据拥有全部权利，OSS应配合将数据转移至新供应商。但Iron Mountain担忧一旦交出数据，会遭到OSS或其继承者的反诉，因而采取了自我保护策略，拒绝直接交付。与此同时，剧情还出现了一段插曲：一位名叫James Tramel的人声称自己是“正式收购OSS的集团管理合伙人”，并与Nine PBS联系了约一个月，随后却突然失联，最后通过自动回复表示他已与OSS无关。Tramel声称自己是被“欺诈”而收购了这家公司，所有权已回归原主。这一系列混乱的归属争议让数据交付陷入僵局，Nine PBS目前能做的只有尽快争取法院强制令，要求Iron Mountain移交数据，以免档案因储存费用欠缴而被清除。

**数据规模与历史价值**  
Nine PBS副总裁兼首席内容官Leah Freeman对媒体表示，这些数据代表了“我们组织70年的历史”，是独一无二、不可替代的社区记录。50TB的存量虽然在大数据时代并不算庞大，但对于一家公共电视台而言，涵盖了数十年来新闻录像、文化节目、地方历史文献等重要内容。文章作者调侃道，即使是一个大型机构，也可以轻松购买一台六盘位NAS并配上大容量机械硬盘来本地备份，而Nine PBS似乎没有这样做。这显然违背了业界经典的“3-2-1备份规则”——即数据应保留三份副本、存放在两种不同介质上，且其中至少一份位于异地。相比之下，韩国政府去年遭遇了数据中心火灾，烧毁了858TB的数据，足以说明单一存储方案的毁灭性风险。

**行业影响与警示**  
这起事件深刻揭示了云存储时代的信任悖论：当组织将数据托管给第三方时，虽然获得了便利和成本优势，但同时也将数据的可用性和安全完全押注于服务商的生存状况。OSS的突然消失并非个案，中小型云存储厂商因经营不善、资金链断裂而倒闭，往往没有妥善的破产交接流程，导致客户数据随之下落不明。尤其当上游服务商（如Iron Mountain）与直接客户之间缺乏明确的法律协议时，数据所有权的边界变得模糊，最终受害的是真正的内容所有者。对于广播档案、科研数据、医疗记录等需要长期保存的信息，单纯依赖“云上保存”并不等于“永久保存”，必须建立多层级、多维度的备份体系，并在合同中明确数据可移植性及异常情况下的救济措施。目前Nine PBS仍在为夺回自己的历史数据而诉讼，这起案件也为所有依赖第三方存储的组织敲响了警钟：在数字时代，保护数据的第一步，是永远不要将唯一的希望寄托于他人之手。

items.title: Elon Musk says xAI will increase data center capacity 7x by 2027 — targeting 10 gigawatts of compute, up to $500 billion in revenue by the end of next year
items.description: Elon Musk expects xAI to increase its nameplate power draw to 10 GW by late 2027, which will increase its performance by orders of magnitude what is available to AI today.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Elon Musk told employees of SpaceX that the power capacity of the company's xAI data centers will increase by 7x to 10GW by late 2027. If this happens, the company's data centers will bring the company some $300 billion – $500 billion in revenue per year, according to Musk. The claim comes as SpaceX's market capitalization dropped by nearly $570 billion in less than two months. Meanwhile, the combined performance of the cluster will by far outpace not only all supercomputers in the Top 500, but also all AI clusters running today.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)Photonics and high-speed data movement is the next big AI bottleneckThe data center cooling state of playMassive AI data center buildouts are squeezing energy suppliesUltra Ethernet: The data center interconnection of tomorrow"We have already built the most powerful AI training clusters in the world," Musk told SpaceX employees at a meeting. "What we expect to do by the end of next year is about 10 times more than what we have done thus far. […] So, we are aiming to get to 10 GW [of compute] by the end of next year. […] If the value per watt is probably going to be $30 to $50, which means if we bring 10 GW of AI compute online by the end of next year, it will be $300 to $500 billion a year in revenue. Big numbers."A lot of powerAt present, SpaceX's xAI data centers in Memphis and Southaven have a rated power draw of 1.4 GW. The company plans to increase the electrical capacity of its data centers to 10 GW by the end of 2027, or by around sevenfold in roughly 1.5 years. It should be noted that AI infrastructure with a 'nameplate power draw' of 1.4 GW by far does not offer compute capacity of 1.4 GW.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: A large AI data center with a power usage effectiveness (PUE) of roughly 1.2 would have around 1.17 GW available to IT equipment (i.e., 230 MW is used by cooling, pumps, fans, humidification/dehumidification, lighting, power distribution losses, UPS losses, and other facility systems). Not all of that 1.17 GW goes to AI accelerators: CPUs, memory, networking, and storage consume a meaningful share. If perhaps 70% – 80% of IT power ultimately corresponds to accelerators, we might be looking at roughly 0.8 GW – 0.95 GW of accelerator power in the case of a 1.4 GW data center.Loads of FLOPSCompute capacity is not measured in Watts; it is measured in floating-point operations per second (FLOPS). Keeping in mind that currently xAI uses a mix of Hopper- and Blackwell-based accelerators, it is hard to determine how much compute xAI has today. Since xAI seems to be betting primarily at Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems from now on, we can make a more or less educated guess about the company's Rubin-based compute capability the company will have by the end of 2027. Actual Rubin AI accelerators will get between 4.816 GW and 5.504 GW of power depending on how much of the IT power will correspond to these GPUs. Each Rubin GPU is expected to consume 2.3 kW of power in Max-P configuration. As a result, xAI's clusters will house between 2.094 million and 2.393 million Rubin GPUs in Max-P mode, or 29,083 and 33,236 NVL72 VR200 systems.The performance of the NVL72 VR200 system is well known, so depending on the number of these machines that xAI will deploy by the end of 2027, we are looking at rather formidable numbers. NVFP4 inference performance of the cluster will be between 105 and 120 ExaFLOPS; NVFP4 training performance will range from 73 to 84 ExaFLOPS; FP6/FP8 training capability is projected between 37 and 42 EFLOPS, whereas native FP64 compute will total 70 – 80 EFLOPS. The total combined FP64 performance of all systems on the Top 500 list is 18.73 EFLOPS. xAI will have 3.7X – 4.3X more than that if the cluster is deployed. As for AI performance, 105 – 120 NVFP4 EFLOPS inference and 73 – 84 NVFP4 EFLOPS training put this cluster in a whole different league from anything publicly operating right now, meaning that we are talking about dramatically more sophisticated AI models coming. Whether or not the combined xAI compute capability will enable the company to earn $300 billion – $500 billion per year is something that remains to be seen, as SpaceX is not the only company selling compute capacity to AI companies, and the competition will likely be rough.Yet, it is about time for Musk to make comments like this, as after topping $2.44 trillion in market capitalization on June 20, SpaceX dropped to $1.43 trillion on August 1, but rebounded to $1.87 trillion on August 12. items.titleZh: 埃隆·马斯克称xAI到2027年将数据中心容量提高7倍——目标是10吉瓦算力，到明年底实现高达5000亿美元营收
items.descriptionZh:
马斯克在SpaceX员工会议上透露，其旗下xAI数据中心的电力容量将在2027年底前提升至10吉瓦（GW），较目前的1.4吉瓦增长约7倍。他预计这一规模若实现，每年可带来3000亿至5000亿美元的收入。这一言论发表之际，公司市值（报道中称SpaceX，但考虑到SpaceX为私营企业，该数据可能实指xAI或相关实体）在不到两个月内下跌近5700亿美元，从6月20日峰值2.44万亿美元降至8月1日的1.43万亿美元，随后于8月12日回升至1.87万亿美元。

目前，xAI在孟菲斯和南黑文的数据中心额定功率为1.4吉瓦，但这并不等同于实际计算功率。以1.4吉瓦额定功率为例，若电能使用效率（PUE）约为1.2，则IT设备可用功率约1.17吉瓦，其中约230兆瓦用于冷却、水泵、风扇、加湿/除湿、照明及配电损耗等基础设施。剩余的IT功率中，CPU、内存、网络和存储系统又会消耗相当一部分，最终只有约70%至80%真正用于AI加速器，即0.8至0.95吉瓦的加速器功率。

计算能力应以FLOPS（每秒浮点运算次数）衡量。当前xAI混合使用英伟达Hopper和Blackwell架构加速器，难以精确估算现有算力。报道推测，xAI未来将主要部署英伟达Vera Rubin平台。若新增的8.6吉瓦额定功率全部采用NVIDIA NVL72 VR200机架级系统，且PUE保持1.2，则IT功率预算为6.88吉瓦，其中Rubin加速器将获得4.816至5.504吉瓦。每块Rubin GPU在Max-P配置下功耗达2.3千瓦，据此推算，集群将容纳209.4万至239.3万块Rubin GPU，对应约2.9万至3.3万套NVL72 VR200系统。

基于NVL72 VR200的已知性能，整个集群的算力将非常惊人：NVFP4格式的推理性能预计为105至120 ExaFLOPS（百亿亿次浮点运算每秒），训练性能为73至84 ExaFLOPS；FP6/FP8格式的训练能力约37至42 EFLOPS；原生FP64双精度计算能力则达70至80 EFLOPS。作为参照，目前Top500榜单所有超级计算机的FP64综合性能总和仅为18.73 EFLOPS，xAI集群将是其3.7至4.3倍。而在AI专用性能（如NVFP4）上，这一集群将远超当前任何公开运行的AI计算设施，意味着未来可以训练和运行比现有模型复杂得多的AI系统，可能推动人工智能在自然语言处理、多模态推理、科学模拟等领域的重大突破。

不过，这些数字均为基于Max-P配置的粗略估算，实际性能可能因系统功耗模式、散热约束及网络瓶颈而有所折扣。至于该集群能否真正带来每年3000亿至5000亿美元的收入，尚需观察——AI算力市场并非xAI一家独大，竞争将相当激烈。马斯克之所以选择此时发声，或许意在提振市场信心，但巨额电力基础设施的建设成本、能源供应压力以及技术演进风险，仍将决定这一宏伟目标的最终实现程度。

items.title: Cerebras shares plunge nearly 20% after missing earnings expectations — hardware sales drop but AI cloud revenue climbs 281%
items.description: Cerebras keeps growing, but misses forecast as hardware sales dip amid explosive increase of AI cloud revenue.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Cerebras on Wednesday reported its financial results for the second quarter, and while its earnings nearly doubled year-over-year, its shares plunged more than 18% in after-hours trading as it missed analysts' expectations, Reuters reports. Furthermore, the company's financial results suggest that Cerebras is increasingly succeeding at selling compute delivered by its hardware, rather than the hardware itself.Tom's Hardware Premium Roadmaps (Image credit: Future)High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) Roadmap Nvidia Enterprise GPU and CPU RoadmapAI accelerator RoadmapDesktop GPU Roadmap3D NAND RoadmapFor the quarter ended June 30, 2026, Cerebras reported revenue of $180.11 million, up from $103.32 million in Q2 2025. Earnings of the company's cloud services totaled $125.99 million, up dramatically from 33.03 million in the same quarter a year ago, but sales of hardware dropped to $54.12 million from $70.3 million in Q2 2025. Wall Street analysts expected Cerebras to earn $194.23 million during the quarter.During the quarter, Cerebras' operating expenses rose to $502.79 million (up from $89.28 million a year ago), its gross margin dropped to 14%, and it lost roughly $450.53 million. The main reason behind the company's skyrocketing operating expenses and losses is stock-based compensation triggered by its May IPO. Once the IPO happened, the company had to recognize the value of stock-based compensation as its expenses, as stock-based compensation jumped from $13.3 million in Q2 2025 to $377 million in Q2 2025. Without the stock-based compensation, the company's net loss would be $73.53 million.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: That said, the analysts were not disappointed by the huge loss, but rather by the earnings miss, the rapidly dropping hardware sales, and uncertain returns generated by Cerebras' new business model.Missing earnings expectations for an AI hardware company amid the AI market frenzy is not a thing that happens often. But perhaps more importantly is that Cerebras' hardware sales dropped 23% year-over-year, whereas cloud and other services revenue skyrocketed by 281%. On the one hand, this proves that the company's clients are more willing to buy its compute hardware in the cloud rather than own it, which means stable revenue streams. However, Cerebras' new business model requires Cerebras to put enormous amounts of capital into infrastructure before it can earn its cloud revenue. You may like Memory maker SK hynix's profit rises 557% amid global shortage, expansion costs climb to $27 billion AMD and Cerebras partner on low-latency, high-throughput AI inference Nvidia no longer reports gaming GPU sales as a separate segment Under its original hardware model, Cerebras has to manufacture its Wafer Scale Engines at TSMC, assemble systems on its base, and sell its CS systems to customers, which then own the machines, install them in their own or leased data centers, and assume the cost of operating the infrastructure. Under its new model, Cerebras retains and deploys the hardware itself, secures data-center capacity and power, and operates the infrastructure, while customers pay Cerebras for access to AI inference/training compute over time rather than buying the machines outright. Without any doubt, demand for inference AI compute is enormous these days, and Cerebras' results prove it. However, the question is whether the company can produce attractive and sustainable profits on the capital it spends on hardware and infrastructure.The $20 billion OpenAI agreement is one example of the business model. Cerebras has committed to provide 750 MW of inference capacity over several years, and OpenAI has an option for another 1.25 GW. As a result, Cerebras must fund 750 MW of infrastructure buildout in advance and opt for another 1.25 GW well before it gets actual money from the AI giant. items.titleZh: Cerebras shares plunge nearly 20% after missing earnings expectations — hardware sales drop but AI cloud revenue climbs 281%
items.descriptionZh:
Cerebras于周三发布了截至2026年6月30日的第二季度财报。尽管营收几乎同比增长了一倍，但由于未能达到华尔街分析师的预期，其股价在盘后交易中暴跌超过18%。据路透社报道，本季度营收为1.8011亿美元，高于去年同期的1.0332亿美元。其中，云服务收入从去年同期的3303万美元飙升至1.2599亿美元，而硬件销售收入则从7030万美元下降至5412万美元，同比减少23%。分析师此前预计Cerebras本季度营收可达1.9423亿美元。

Cerebras本季度运营费用大幅攀升至5.0279亿美元，去年同期为8928万美元；毛利率下滑至14%，净亏损约4.5053亿美元。运营费用和亏损激增的主要原因是5月IPO触发的股权激励支出——该类支出从去年同期的1330万美元跃升至本季度的3.77亿美元。如果剔除这部分非现金支出，公司净亏损实际为7353万美元。分析师的不满并非源于巨额亏损本身，而是营收未达预期、硬件销售快速下滑，以及公司新商业模式带来的不确定回报。

财报数据折射出一个重要趋势：Cerebras正越来越多地通过销售硬件所承载的计算力来获利，而非直接出售硬件本身。硬件收入同比下降23%，而云及其他服务收入激增281%，这证明客户更倾向于按需租用算力而非购置自有设备，使公司获得更稳定的经常性收入。然而，这一新商业模式要求Cerebras在获得云收入之前，先期投入巨额资金建设基础设施。

在原有硬件模式下，Cerebras在台积电制造晶圆级引擎（Wafer Scale Engine），自行组装系统，然后将完整的CS系统出售给客户，由客户自行拥有机器、部署在自有或租赁的数据中心，并承担运营成本。而在新模式下，Cerebras保留了硬件所有权并自行部署，获取数据中心容量和电力，负责基础设施运营；客户则按使用时长付费，获得AI推理/训练算力，而无需一次性购买机器。当前AI推理算力需求巨大，Cerebras的业绩也印证了这一点，但关键在于，公司是否能在投入的硬件和基础设施资本之上产生有吸引力且可持续的利润。

与OpenAI签订的200亿美元协议就是这一商业模式的典型例证。Cerebras承诺在数年内提供750MW的推理容量，OpenAI还拥有额外1.25GW的选购权。这意味着Cerebras必须先期投入资金完成750MW基础设施的建设，并在真正从OpenAI获得收入前，就要决定是否追加1.25GW的投资。尽管OpenAI通过约10亿美元的有担保营运资金贷款帮助Cerebras融资，但Cerebras仍需在多个季度乃至数年内持续投入资金，之后才能开始确认收入。这种资本密集、回报滞后的模型，正是市场对其商业模式可持续性产生疑虑的核心所在。

items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 8 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Qualcomm is getting into some of the nitty-gritty details of the Snapdragon C system-on-a-chip, the ARM-based platform it announced in June for laptops priced around $300.The Snapdragon C is an 8-core Qualcomm Kryo CPU, with a single-core max frequency of 3 GHz and a multi-core max of 2 GHz. (In the fine print, Qualcomm claims you can get four cores at 2.0 GHz and three cores at 2.6 GHz, but doesn't note all eight cores simultaneously. We've reached out to Qualcomm for clarification. There is 2MB of total cache.It also has an integrated Adreno GPU with a max frequency of 900 MHz, and a Qualcomm Hexagon NPU, though Qualcomm hasn't listed how many TOPS it supports. Swipe to scroll horizontally Qualcomm Snapdragon C Header Cell - Column 1 CPU 8-core Qualcomm Kryo CPU Single-core max frequency 3.0 GHz Multi-core max frequnecy 2.0 GHz Total cache 2 MB GPU Qualcomm Adreno GPU (integrated) NPU Qualcomm Hexagon, no TOPS metric specified Memory support Up to 16GB LPDDR5/5x or LPDDR4x Storage PCIe 3.0 NVMe, UFS 2.2/3.1 Wi-Fi Qualcomm FastConnect C6700 (up to Wi-Fi 6/6E) USB Up to USB 3.1, up to 2x USB-C, 2x USB-A In updated slides, Qualcomm pits the Snapdragon C (in a reference design with 8GB of memory) against an Acer TravelMate with Intel's N250 and 8GB of RAM. The company claims you get 67% better battery performance than the Intel N250 and up to 2.1 times better battery efficiency, though that's measured with multi-threaded Cinebench. The company did not publish any benchmarks when the systems are plugged in.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: (Image credit: Qualcomm)Qualcomm claims that, on battery, the Snapdragon C is up to 44% faster in single-threaded Geekbench and 24% higher in multi-core. But its top victories were in Cinebench, running 50% faster single-threaded and 67% faster multi-threaded. But Geekbench and Speedometer 3.1 (+39%) are the real numbers to look at here, as they better showcase the type of work someone might typically do with a cheap notebook. (Image credit: Qualcomm)While Qualcomm is promising "all-day" battery life, it's leaving the number of hours up to its OEM partners. That's likely to vary depending on the display panels and other factors, but in Qualcomm's test reference device, it used a 16-inch screen. Qualcomm notes in its footnotes that the TravelMate has an 11.6-inch display, with "total power configured to match 16" screen."Qualcomm instead is claiming battery power efficiency over the Intel N250 across all of its tests, from Netflix running in Microsoft Edge (106% better), web browsing (68% better), and a Teams video call (74% better). 高通公司近日公布了其面向约300美元价位笔记本电脑设计的ARM架构系统级芯片（SoC）Snapdragon C的更多技术细节。该平台于今年六月首次发布，目标是将ARM架构引入廉价笔记本市场，与英特尔的低端处理器展开直接竞争。根据高通最新披露的参数，Snapdragon C集成了8核Qualcomm Kryo CPU，最高单核频率可达3GHz，多核最高频率为2GHz。不过在高通的注释中，具体核心配置为4个2.0GHz核心加3个2.6GHz核心，并未明确所有8个核心能否同时工作在高频状态。芯片配备2MB总缓存。图形方面集成了Adreno GPU，最高频率900MHz，并集成Qualcomm Hexagon NPU，但高通尚未提供其算力（TOPS）数值。内存支持最高16GB LPDDR5/5x或LPDDR4x，存储支持PCIe 3.0 NVMe固态硬盘及UFS 2.2/3.1，连接性包括FastConnect C6700（支持Wi-Fi 6/6E）、USB 3.1、双USB-C和双USB-A接口。

在性能对比方面，高通将Snapdragon C（8GB内存参考设计）与配备Intel N250和8GB内存的宏碁TravelMate笔记本进行比较，声称其电池续航性能比Intel N250提升67%，电池效率提升最高2.1倍，这一数据基于多线程Cinebench测试。在电池模式下，Geekbench单核成绩快44%，多核成绩快24%；Cinebench单核成绩快50%，多核快67%；Speedometer 3.1浏览器性能测试快39%。高通强调这些测试更能反映廉价笔记本用户的典型使用场景。尽管高通承诺“全天”电池续航，但未给出具体小时数，因为这将取决于OEM合作伙伴的屏幕等配置。在测试参考设备中使用了16英寸屏幕，而对比的TravelMate为11.6英寸，但高通表示其“总功耗配置为匹配16英寸屏幕”。此外，高通还列出了多项实际应用场景的能效提升：在Microsoft Edge中播放Netflix时能效提升106%，网页浏览提升68%，Teams视频通话提升74%。

高通已确认惠普、宏碁、华硕和联想将推出搭载Snapdragon C的产品。在Computex上，宏碁首次展示了其搭载Snapdragon C的笔记本Aspire Go 15，配备8GB RAM、512GB存储和丰富的端口，但尚未公布发售日期和价格。市场分析认为，OEM合作伙伴可能选择在柏林IFA展会或明年初CES上发布新品。值得注意的是，受内存等组件成本上涨影响，此前300美元的定价目标能否维持尚存疑问。如果价格策略能够落地，Snapdragon C笔记本有望在性价比上大幅优于苹果MacBook Neo以及搭载Intel Wildcat Lake的Windows笔记本。但实际性能表现仍需等待实机测试验证。

history.title: Near-packaged optics (NPO) gains ground as the industry hedges against CPO's growing pains — analysts say volume for NPO silicon photonics products will extend until the end of the decade
history.description: The case for near-packaged optics (NPO) is strengthening, as the growing pains of co-packaged optics (CPO) become apparent. We explain the material differences between the two technologies as optics and silicon photonics make waves in the AI industry.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter SemiAnalysis made the case for near-packaged optics (NPO) in a three-part thread posted to X on August 10, describing the architecture as an interim solution for the industry's transition from pluggable transceivers to true co-packaged optics (CPO) and crediting it with three advantages: field-replaceable modules, a failure blast radius confined to a single socketed unit, and simpler assembly, since the optical engine is packaged separately from the switch ASIC.Just two months ago, SemiAnalysis published a research note pushing its CPO volume expectations out to 2027 for scale-out networks and 2028 or 2029 for full-scale production, subsequently knocking 17% off Applied Optoelectronics stock and roughly 8% off Lumentum in a single session and drawing a public rebuttal from rival analysts.NPO is the architecture that stands to gain if that pessimism proves right, with Broadcom having shown a 3.2T VCSEL-based NPO product line at OFC 2026 in March, and six connector and optics firms forming a standards group the same week to define a common socket for this class of device.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: NPO presents an interim solution under the transition from pluggable to true CPO. NPO has certain benefits over CPO that bypass current production and reliability challenge of CPO, while maintaining most of the benefits CPO provide.Pros:🟠 Better serviceability (field… pic.twitter.com/R4JQX2xeQAAugust 10, 2026NPO vs CPO and pluggable opticsA front-panel pluggable transceiver sits 15cm to 30 cm of copper trace away from the switch ASIC, and the DSP that cleans up the signal after that journey draws 6W to 8W of a typical 800G module's 14 to 17W budget. CPO reduces that distance to millimeters by mounting the optical engine on the same package substrate as the ASIC, thereby eliminating the DSP. Per Broadcom, this enabled a 70% reduction in optics power for its co-packaged Tomahawk switches, and Nvidia's figures for a 1.6T link show per-link power falling from around 30W to 9W.NPO splits the difference by moving the optical engine off the faceplate to sit beside the ASIC, close enough to shorten the electrical path and drop the DSP, but on its own engine substrate instead of the ASIC's package. The module mates to the board through a socket, so the engine can be pulled and replaced in the field in the same way that a pluggable can; an engine reflowed onto a CPO substrate can't. SemiAnalysis's January CPO deep dive defines NPO as an optical engine co-packaged onto a separate substrate that "remains socketable." You may like Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity How optical interconnects and silicon photonics emerged as AI's next hot commodity Lumentum CEO warns of impending bottleneck on critical material used for silicon photonics Linear pluggable optics (LPO), the other interim architecture in circulation, takes the opposite route by removing the DSP but leaving the optics in a standard front-panel module, cutting power to roughly seven to 8.5W per 800G port at the cost of reach and interoperability headaches, while leaving the optical engine on the faceplate rather than moving it next to the ASIC.Serviceability and yield A soldered CPO substrate has no rework path because removing a reflowed, underfilled engine means applying solder-melt temperatures of 220°C to 260°C millimeters from the ASIC and every other engine on the package, and the sub-micron fiber alignment inside the engine itself doesn't survive a second thermal excursion. One dead optical engine therefore condemns the switch ASIC, the substrate, and every other engine attached to it.SemiAnalysis's June note ran the numbers for a hypothetical 32-engine package. At a 95% attach yield per engine, compound yield lands near 19%, or roughly one good assembly in five. GlobalSemiResearch published a point-by-point rebuttal arguing the calculation freezes yield at a single pessimistic snapshot and ignores screening, binning, and the spare engines Nvidia designed into Spectrum-X for redundancy.Meta presented reliability results at OFC 2026 indicating co-packaged optics can beat pluggables on failure rates, and Broadcom said its CPO systems logged more than 1 million cumulative 400G-equivalent port-hours in Meta testing without a single link flap.Lasers, historically the highest-failure optical component, sit outside the package in both architectures: the OIF's ELSFP standard, published in August 2023, defines a hot-swappable external laser module that CPO and NPO designs both draw on. Modulators, photodetectors, and fiber attach stay inside the engine, so a failure in any of those means either swapping a socketed module or scrapping a soldered one. What to read next Inside optical and the battle for scale FCC proposes import ban on Chinese optical transceivers Elon Musk receives FTC greenlight to buy Mesh Optical as interconnects emerge as AI's tightest bottleneck Shipping products and roadmaps Nvidia's Quantum-X Photonics InfiniBand switch, which entered production deployments this year, carries 144 ports of 800G across 18 silicon photonics engines mounted on detachable optical sub-assemblies, with 18 removable external laser modules feeding them. Nvidia markets the design as CPO, but engines that unbolt from the package and lasers that slide out of the faceplate are the serviceability properties SemiAnalysis assigns to NPO. The Ethernet counterpart, Spectrum-X Photonics, is due in the second half of this year at up to 512 ports of 800G.Broadcom runs both architectures side by side. Its 51.2T Bailly CPO switch has been in volume production at system partner Micas Networks since 2024, its 102.4T Tomahawk 6 Davisson began customer deliveries in October last year; and at OFC 2026 it added the 3.2T VCSEL-based NPO line as a separate offering aimed at buyers who want density without the soldered commitment.Foxconn Interconnect Technology has had solderless LGA-to-LGA sockets and pluggable laser-source cages for Bailly in full production since May last year, and Ciena, Coherent, Marvell, Molex, Samtec, and TeraHop launched the Open CPX MSA at OFC 2026 to standardize a socketed optical-engine interface covering both NPO and CPO. LightCounting CEO Vladimir Kozlov, quoted in the MSA's launch release, put the stakes at "annual port shipments projected to top 100 million" within five years, against fewer than 1 million co-packaged and near-packaged ports in 2025.TSMC's COUPE optical engine entered mass production this year in its first-generation pluggable form, with the 6.4T co-packaged second generation targeted around 2027 and a third generation moving optics inside the processor package itself. If those dates hold, NPO's run as the interim architecture lasts two to three years. If SemiAnalysis's 2029 scale-up timeline proves closer to reality, however, NPO carries the volume for the rest of the decade, adding demand to a photonics supply chain that's already short of lasers and packaging capacity.

history.titleZh: Near-packaged optics (NPO) gains ground as the industry hedges against CPO's growing pains — analysts say volume for NPO silicon photonics products will extend until the end of the decade
history.descriptionZh:
今年8月10日，SemiAnalysis在X平台发布三篇系列推文，力推"近封装光学"（NPO）技术路线，将其定位为行业从可插拔光模块向真正共封装光学（CPO）过渡的中间方案。就在两个月前，SemiAnalysis曾发布研报，将CPO的大规模部署预期推迟至2027年（scale-out网络）乃至2028至2029年（全面量产），该报告当日导致Applied Optoelectronics股价下跌17%、Lumentum下跌约8%，并引发竞争对手分析师的公开反驳。如果这一悲观判断被证实，NPO正是最可能受益的架构——博通已在2026年3月的OFC大会上展示了基于VCSEL的3.2T NPO产品线，同周六家连接器和光学厂商成立标准组织，共同定义该类器件的统一插座接口。

**NPO与CPO、可插拔光模块的架构对比**

传统的前面板可插拔收发器距离交换ASIC有15至30厘米的铜走线距离，承担信号修复任务的DSP功耗达6至8瓦，占典型800G模块14至17瓦总功耗的近一半。CPO将光学引擎直接安装在ASIC同一封装基板上，把距离缩短至毫米级，从而省去DSP。据博通数据，其共封装Tomahawk交换机的光学功耗降低了70%；英伟达的1.6T链路数据显示，每链路功耗从约30瓦降至9瓦。NPO则采取折中路线：将光学引擎从面板移至ASIC旁边，缩短电路路径并去掉DSP，但引擎安装在独立基板上而非ASIC的封装上。模块通过插座与电路板连接，因此可以像可插拔模块一样在现场插拔更换，而回流焊在CPO基板上的引擎则无法做到。SemiAnalysis在一月份的CPO深度报告中定义NPO为"共封装在独立基板上且保持可插拔性"的光学引擎。

另一种过渡架构——线性可插拔光学（LPO）走的是相反路线：去掉DSP但保留标准前面板模块形态，将800G端口功耗降至约7至8.5瓦，代价是传输距离缩短和互操作性难题，且光学引擎仍留在面板而非移近ASIC。

**可维护性与良率问题**

焊接式CPO基板没有返修路径：移除回流焊并经过底部填充的光学引擎需要在距ASIC和其他引擎仅数毫米处施加220°C至260°C的焊料熔化温度，而引擎内部亚微米级的光纤对准无法承受第二次热冲击。因此，一个光学引擎损坏就意味着交换ASIC、基板及所有其他引擎全部报废。SemiAnalysis六月的报告以一个假设的32引擎封装为例进行计算：在单个引擎95%的贴装良率下，复合良率仅约19%，即大约五套组装中只有一套合格。GlobalSemiResearch则发布逐点反驳，认为该计算将良率冻结在单一的悲观快照上，忽略了筛选、分档以及英伟达为Spectrum-X设计的冗余备用引擎。

Meta在OFC 2026上公布的可靠性数据显示，CPO在故障率上可以优于可插拔方案；博通称其CPO系统在Meta测试中累计运行超过100万小时的400G等效端口小时，未出现一次链路抖动。激光器历来是故障率最高的光学元件，在两种架构中均置于封装外部：OIF于2023年8月发布的ELSFP标准定义了可热插拔的外部激光模块，CPO和NPO设计均可采用。调制器、光电探测器和光纤耦合组件则留在引擎内部，这些部件一旦故障，要么更换插拔式模块，要么报废焊接式封装。

**产品布局与路线图**

英伟达的Quantum-X Photonics InfiniBand交换机今年已进入生产部署阶段，搭载144个800G端口，由18个安装在可拆卸光学子组件上的硅光子引擎驱动，并配备18个可拆卸外部激光模块。英伟达将其定位为CPO，但引擎可从封装上拆下、激光器可从面板滑出——这些正是SemiAnalysis归为NPO的可维护性特征。对应的以太网版本Spectrum-X Photonics计划今年下半年推出，最高支持512个800G端口。

博通则并行推进两种架构：51.2T的Bailly CPO交换机自2024年起已由系统合作伙伴Micas Networks量产，102.4T的Tomahawk 6 Davisson于去年10月开始向客户交付；在OFC 2026上，博通新增了基于VCSEL的3.2T NPO产品线，面向希望获得高密度又不想承担焊接式承诺的买家。

富士康互连技术（Foxconn Interconnect Technology）自去年5月起已全面量产适用于Bailly的无焊LGA-to-LGA插座和可插拔激光源笼。Ciena、Coherent、Marvell、Molex、Samtec和TeraHop六家公司在OFC 2026上发起Open CPX MSA，旨在标准化覆盖NPO和CPO的插座式光学引擎接口。LightCounting首席执行官Vladimir Kozlov在该MSA发布时表示，五年内年度端口出货量预计将突破1亿个，而2025年共封装和近封装端口总出货量不足100万个。

台积电的COUPE光学引擎今年已以第一代可插拔形态进入量产，第二代6.4T共封装版本目标在2027年左右推出，第三代则计划将光学元件直接集成到处理器封装内部。如果这些时间节点兑现，NPO作为过渡架构的存续期约为两到三年。但如果SemiAnalysis所预测的2029年规模化时间表更接近现实，NPO将在本十年余下时间内承担出货主力，为本已面临激光器和封装产能短缺的光子供应链带来额外需求。

history.content: Suno is releasing Studio 2.0 with significant upgrades that push it closer to an actual digital audio workstation (DAW), rather than a bare-bones audio editor with generative AI features. The biggest addition is undoubtedly MIDI support. Suno says that MIDI was its most requested feature, and it’s basically a prerequisite for any modern DAW. Unfortunately, Suno Studio doesn’t appear to support third-party plugins or VSTs yet, so you’re stuck using its proprietary built-in synth. That synth appears to be a basic two-oscillator wavetable plugin with three envelopes and four LFOs.The point is less about using your favorite Arturia vintage synth emulation, though, and more about using that MIDI data as a prompt. You can play in some chords, then ask Suno to turn that MIDI into audio, extend a melody, or write a B-part based on what you played. Another standard DAW feature being added in Studio 2.0 is automation. So now you can pan or change the volume of individual tracks across the arrangement.Suno is also adding a chatbot to the Studio interface so you can prompt it for lyrics or a new guitar line. This isn’t an isolated generator either, it is tied into the current session and pulls in the musical context of your current project. So you can tell it things like “make this vocal track sound better,” and it will add reverb, compression, and EQ. Oh, and yes, Suno Studio now has a suite of simple built-in effects, including distortion, delay, reverb, compression, and EQ.The most interesting feature of the chat interface, however, is the ability to create custom effects plugins. These can be unique reverbs, brickwalled compression, or chorus effects, similar to Polyend’s Endless AI guitar pedal. These effects are saved to your account as well, so they can be reused at a later date.Suno Studio 2.0 is a lot more feature-packed than version one, but the beta version of the chat leaves even less to do for the users. In the demo above, Suno’s Henry Phipps can be seen cleaning up some flubbed notes and quantizing MIDI, before saying he should be asking the chatbot to do all this for him. He also leaves deciding on a vocal chain up to the AI rather than selecting effects himself.Suno Studio is starting to look more like an actual DAW. Image: SunoCorrection August 13th: This story originally stated Suno’s built-in synth had four envelopes instead of four LFOs.
